note: Quarantine and deferred-scope ledger (closure plan §5.2). The draft landed in Slice 0; S2 added the machine-readable validator (e2e/real/manifest.spec.ts), which now enforces the entry contract, forbids silent `test.fixme` quarantine, and requires every deferred scope to carry an owner and an unlock. The `baseline` block below is the frozen Slice 0 reference, not the current tally.

baseline.protocol: 2 rounds same-order + 1 round reversed per-file invocation; workers=1, retries=0, no sleep, no waits
baseline.result: 13 stable failures (identical sets in rounds 1-2) + 1 single-occurrence flake; bench 59/60 green with 1 stable narrow failure

chat.e3: asset categories, composer submit, session routes

coding.e4: landed: session turn + restart durability, files search/read/traversal, PTY create/stream/exit/delete (e2e/real/session-{turn,files,pty}.spec.ts)

custom.e3: builder states + typed negative gate (kill switch off)
custom.e4: planned S9C (typed negative first, approved-env happy path later)

v2-runtime-execution-gap.scope: V2 durable admission admits but never dispatches provider work and the V1-shaped projection is empty (flag default off; custom always V2). Pinned live by e2e/real/v2-admission-gap.spec.ts — green there means the gap is still present.
v2-runtime-execution-gap.unlock: Owner ruling before S9C starts: complete V2 execution (separate authorisation, touches durable-admission invariants) or re-scope S9C's positive path to admission + snapshot lifecycle with the turn gap recorded as residual

provider-scenario-scripts.scope: streaming success + tool-call/HTTP-failure/SSE-interruption/duplicate/slow scripts. S5 landed the streaming-success script (orchestrator provider) plus /e4/provider-requests dispatch evidence; the remaining scenarios stay unwritten until a spec needs them
provider-scenario-scripts.unlock: each remaining scenario (tool call, HTTP failure, SSE interruption, duplicate/out-of-order, slow response) is added with the spec that needs it — the real consumer is S9A (plan §12.4 requires provider failure/recovery E4)

break-glass-bar-entry.scope: the status bar projects permission state but offers no entry into the break-glass control surface; the lease owner (30s renew / 60s lease) lives in the composer and duplicating it in the bar would create the second truth source ADR-23 forbids
break-glass-bar-entry.unlock: S12 final review must rule on the shared permission control surface (this entry and permission-tier-mutation-entry ride on the same owner extraction). Either fund that slice — refactor the lease owner out of the composer, then attach both the break-glass entry and the tier mutation entry — or record an explicit product decision that the app has no break-glass entry. It may not pass silently.

agent-picker-custom-narrowing.scope: the picker no longer hides when showCustomAgents is off, but narrowing the list to official agents still needs asset provenance (AgentV2.Info.originRelativePath) in the /agent payload, which the instance endpoint does not serve today
agent-picker-custom-narrowing.unlock: add origin provenance to the /agent response projection (same shape the V2 agent registry sets via core/agent/asset-bridge.ts), then the setting can mean 'include extra custom agents' as ruled

permission-tier-mutation-entry.scope: the resident PermissionTierSelector is deleted (plan §9.2), so the app currently has no UI entry that changes a session's tier. Plan §9.2 intended relocation into a control surface, not a bare deletion — that gap is a product fact, not a detail. The data path is intact: submit still carries permissionTier at creation, drafts keep their persisted value, the server field is unchanged and the projection still reads it.
permission-tier-mutation-entry.unlock: S12 final review must rule: fund the shared permission control surface (one owner extraction shared with break-glass-bar-entry, not two) or explicitly accept 'no tier-change UI' as a recorded product decision. Until then no release note may imply the tier is editable in-app.

session-product-header-projection.scope: plan §9.2 opens with a shared Session Header projecting mode, Location/scope, agent/model source, permission, mode-specific identity and health from the same ADR-23 projection, and §9.3 asks for an E3 row across all five modes. S6 landed the projection and its StatusBar and agent-picker consumers; the Header is not delivered. packages/app/src/components/session/session-header.tsx is OS window chrome (titlebar mounts), not an identity surface, so nothing today shows identity or health at session level. It gates S9B: Assistant M1 (plan §13.1) requires the Header to carry its scope contract.
session-product-header-projection.unlock: run it as its own small slice before S9B starts: first the product ruling on which surface carries session-level identity/health (Owner-deferred question, not an implementation choice), then feed it from SessionIdentityProjection with no UI-side inference and no second truth source, then the §9.3 five-mode E3 row

identity-e4-cross-server-and-historical.scope: plan §9.3 asks E4 for refresh, cross-server and historical Session. Refresh landed (e2e/real/session-identity-consumers.spec.ts reload case). Cross-server isolation and pre-identity-era historical sessions have unit/E3 coverage only: the projection is rebuilt per request from Location-scoped services, so reuse across servers is structurally impossible, but no E4 case exercises two backends or a session created before the fields existed.
identity-e4-cross-server-and-historical.unlock: land with S9A's E4 expansion (which already adds provider failure/recovery): a second backend plus a historical seed, asserting the projection does not leak across server or Location boundaries

identity-narrow-viewport-controls.scope: plan §9.2 requires the new agent picker and permission state to stay keyboard-reachable and fully readable at narrow widths, with long lists scrolling rather than squeezing the model and submit controls. S6's E3 coverage for these controls runs at the default viewport only.
identity-narrow-viewport-controls.unlock: land with S7's narrow-screen and keyboard a11y slice: a chromium-narrow case asserting keyboard reach, full accessible name and that the picker's growth does not displace model or submit
